text: Figure 2.25: Logical view of multi-partition service modules Following the general concept of the BSW multi-core distribution, the service compo- nent merely offers its services on multiple partitions. From a logical and execution con- text point of view, the service component exists (lives) in multiple partitions. That does however not mean, that the component’s code or data must be multiplied. The same code can be executed on multiple partitions. Interfaces to neighboring BSW modules remain unchanged and are kept on one partition to maintain backward compatibility to the rest of the BSW stack. Potential existing requirements for BSW multi-core distribu- tion that need to be fulfilled by the component will remain unchanged as well. This architecture-pattern uses the AUTOSAR Master-Satellite-approach towards the application (RTE) while it keeps the API compatibility towards neighboring BSW mod- ules. If or if not a BSW service component implements this design pattern is implementation specific. T echnically there is no need to do so because the RTE is capable to provide all required cross-partition/core communication between application SWC and BSW. Implementation of this pattern is hence merely an optimization.
